related_questions.question: What does it mean when my non-HDL cholesterol is high?

text_blocks.snippet: High non-HDL cholesterol levels indicate an increased risk of heart disease, as it includes all the "bad" cholesterol, like LDL and VLDL, that can contribute to atherosclerosis (plaque buildup in arteries). High non-HDL cholesterol, particularly when combined with low HDL (good) cholesterol, is a strong predictor of cardiovascular events such as heart attack and stroke.
snippet_highlighted_words: an increased risk of heart disease

list.title: What is non-HDL cholesterol?
list.snippet: It's a calculation of all the cholesterol in the blood that isn't carried by HDL (good) cholesterol. This includes LDL (bad) cholesterol, VLDL (very low-density lipoprotein) cholesterol, and other lipoproteins that can contribute to plaque buildup in arteries.

list.title: Why is it important?
list.snippet: Non-HDL cholesterol is considered a better indicator of cardiovascular disease risk than just LDL cholesterol alone because it captures all the harmful cholesterol types.

list.title: What are healthy levels?
list.snippet: For most people, a healthy non-HDL cholesterol level is less than 130 mg/dL. For individuals with a history of heart disease, the target may be lower.

list.title: What causes high non-HDL cholesterol?
list.snippet: Several factors can contribute, including a diet high in saturated and trans fats, lack of physical activity, smoking, and being overweight or obese, according to Verywell Health.

list.title: What can you do?
list.snippet: Lifestyle changes like adopting a healthy diet, increasing physical activity, and quitting smoking can help lower non-HDL cholesterol. In some cases, medication may be necessary to manage high cholesterol levels.
